name: Frontal medial cortex
summary: The frontal medial cortex is the medial prefrontal cortex below the anterior cingulate and in front of the subcallosal area, corresponding to the medial part of Brodmann areas 10, 11 and 32 (the ventromedial prefrontal cortex). It integrates the value of choices, regulates emotion through its dense connections with the amygdala and hypothalamus, and forms the anterior hub of the default mode network with the posterior cingulate. It is damaged by anterior cerebral and anterior communicating artery pathology, by subfrontal tumors and by head injury, producing the impulsive, socially inappropriate and poorly regulated behavior classically described after orbitomedial frontal damage.

anatomy.location: Medial surface of the frontal lobe below the cingulate gyrus and anterior to the paraterminal gyrus and the subcallosal area, continuous below with the gyrus rectus and the medial orbital cortex; it faces the falx and the contralateral cortex across the interhemispheric fissure.

afferents.via: uncinate fasciculus and ventral amygdalofugal pathway

function: Ventromedial prefrontal neurons encode the expected value and the emotional consequence of an option and pass this to the anterior cingulate, the striatum and the amygdala, so that decisions are guided by anticipated feelings; without it patients choose immediate gains over long-term benefit and cannot learn from social punishment. The region is also the front of the default mode network active in self-reflection and thinking about other minds, it suppresses the amygdala during extinction of fear, and it modulates autonomic tone through the hypothalamus and the periaqueductal gray. Bilateral loss produces apathy, whereas orbital-medial damage sparing the anterior cingulate produces disinhibition.

bestView.label: medial prefrontal cortex below the cingulate gyrus
ventromedial frontal cortex above the gyrus rectus

imaging.normalAppearance: Cortex on the medial surface of the frontal lobe in front of the genu and below the cingulate sulcus; thin, with variable sulcation, best seen on sagittal images a few millimeters off the midline.

pathology.finding: Subarachnoid blood in the interhemispheric fissure and a hematoma in the medial frontal cortex or gyrus rectus; later infarcts of the basal forebrain.
Enhancing dural mass under the medial frontal lobes with edema tracking along the cingulum and personality change.
Medial and orbital frontal atrophy with a widened interhemispheric fissure anterior to the genu.

lesionEffects.deficit: Impulsivity, poor decision making and social disinhibition
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of value-based decision signals from the ventromedial prefrontal cortex to the striatum and amygdala
Disconnection of the medial prefrontal cortex from the anterior cingulate and hypothalamus

lesionEffects.deficit: Autonomic dysregulation and altered fear extinction
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of prefrontal inhibition of the amygdala and the hypothalamic autonomic outflow

examination: Collateral history of personality change, gambling, tactlessness or new indifference
Bedside social cognition: reading emotion in faces, understanding faux pas
Look for coexisting anosmia and visual field defects when a subfrontal mass is suspected
pearls: The patient with ventromedial frontal damage knows the rules but does not use them; intelligence tests can be normal
Frontal personality change plus anosmia is a subfrontal mass until imaged
Anterior communicating aneurysm patients combine amnesia (basal forebrain) with medial frontal disinhibition

pitfalls: Lesions here can produce a picture indistinguishable from a primary psychiatric illness; a first psychiatric presentation after 40 deserves imaging
